After Static Charge lands, move toward cover so the stun does not guarantee a full damage sequence.
After Static Charge lands, move toward cover so the stun does not guarantee a full damage sequence. Avoid standing beside the wave when it gives his area damage easy value on both you and troopers.
After a knife connects, use cover and let the effect end instead of allowing repeated hits to refresh the pressure.

After a knife connects, use cover and let the effect end instead of allowing repeated hits to refresh the pressure. Keep moving after a full-rage dash so the second hit does not land where you stopped.

After clearing accumulated marks, change the firing angle so Mirage cannot immediately rebuild the same pressure. Punish an offensive Tornado with teammates nearby instead of chasing into another extended weapon exchange.
After he lands, apply movement denial while teammates can punish the exposed position.
After her mobility is spent, close the fight before the next escape window.

After removing Sticky Bomb, move away from his next firing angle rather than treating the cleanse as permission to stay close. Keep a separate response for a vulnerable ultimate channel, especially when his team can punish your approach.
After she spends Stone Form, look for a safe trade while the defensive tool is unavailable.
Against Abrams: Apply Toxic Bullets or another anti-heal source before committing. Percent max-health bleed plus healing reduction attacks both his large health pool and his sustain.

Against Abrams: Buy Reactive Barrier as an early lane stabilizer. Shoulder Charge and other movement-lock effects trigger the barrier and restore stamina, giving you enough protection to survive the immediate melee follow-up.
Against Abrams: Buy Rebuttal and play around your parry. The shorter parry cooldown and melee-focused stats punish the repeated melee pattern Abrams wants.

Against Abrams: Hold Warp Stone or use vertical movement for the engage. Repositioning avoids the control entirely instead of relying on Indomitable, which can be consumed by the first stage of Shoulder Charge.
Against Apollo: Build Spellbreaker or Spirit Resilience. Apollo deals a large amount of front-loaded spirit damage, so spirit defense reduces the part of his combo that actually converts kills.

Against Apollo: Layer Silence Wave after his cleanse or when he commits. If Apollo removes the first movement lock, a silence creates a second shutdown window and prevents him from immediately chaining the abilities that let him escape.
Against Apollo: Time Counterspell for the actual damage window of the ultimate. Correct timing can negate the ability damage and effects even after the sequence has started.
Against Apollo: Use Slowing Hex before he starts the movement sequence. It shuts off a large portion of Apollo's mobility and makes his commit much easier to punish.

Against Baba: use Spirit Sap before a spell trade when her Spirit-scaling pressure is deciding the exchange. Coordinate allied spirit damage while she is affected, and keep a separate response for Threadsap, melee pressure or control.
Against Bebop: Cast Knockdown while he is channeling in the air. The stun can interrupt the channel and the anti-air bonus makes airborne targets easier to punish.
Against Bebop: Use Dispel Magic before detonation. Sticky Bomb is a non-ultimate debuff and can be purged, dropping the bomb instead of eating the full burst.

Against Bebop: Use Divine Barrier on the bombed teammate. It can cleanse removable non-stun debuffs from an ally, making it one of the best team-save answers when the bomb is on someone other than you.
Against Bebop: Use Indomitable for the first hard-control event or Unstoppable proactively. Breaking the hook control prevents the bomb and uppercut follow-up from becoming a full combo.
Against Calico: Build Spirit Resilience or Spellbreaker. Her dangerous burst is heavily spirit-based, so dedicated spirit defense buys time to survive the combo.
Against Calico: Use Cursed Relic when your team is ready to burst. The silence and item lock create the short coordinated window Calico normally denies with mobility and defensive cooldowns.
Against Calico: Use Ethereal Shift during the committed damage window. Invulnerability lets you wait out the most dangerous part of the sequence instead of trying to outrun it.
Against Calico: Use the active movement and stamina denial while your team can finish the catch. Favor it on a build that already values the weapon and farming side of the item.
Against Celeste: Disarm her once she commits. Celeste can function like a gun carry after her abilities create the opening, so turning off the weapon removes a major part of the follow-up.
Against Celeste: Use ability-applied slowing to create a follow-up window. Coordinate damage during that window rather than expecting the slow to secure a kill alone.

Against Drifter: Activate Metal Skin during the committed weapon burst. It gives a temporary bullet-immunity window that can completely waste the part of Drifter's all-in that depends on sustained gun damage.
Against Drifter: Use a weapon-triggered barrier to stabilize the gun follow-up. A cleanse is a separate answer to the mark that enables the teleport.
Against Dynamo: Activate Unstoppable before the expected engage. Indomitable does not reliably free you from Singularity, while proactive CC immunity prevents the control from taking hold.
Against Dynamo: Use Rescue Beam on a trapped teammate from outside the ultimate. Once the channel cannot be interrupted, pulling an ally out becomes one of the few remaining ways to save them.
Against Dynamo: Use extra stamina and vertical movement to jump the knockup pattern. The pulse is ground-oriented, so staying above its timing can deny repeated setup value.
Against Graves: Apply strong anti-heal before the all-in. Graves has meaningful sustain, and cutting the recovery window makes her much easier to finish once her summons are cleared.

Against Graves: Buy Monster Rounds as the cheaper early answer. Extra damage into NPCs and summons helps you clear her spawned pressure sooner instead of letting the wave and ghouls snowball the lane.

Against Graves: Use Ricochet on a weapon build, or Monster Rounds for a more accessible summon-clear option. Clearing grouped summons reduces Graves’s resource pressure, but a weapon investment needs to fit your own hero and build.

Against Grey Talon: Consider Spirit Shielding and stay near hard cover for the next shot. A significant spirit burst can trigger the barrier, helping stabilize the exchange without treating the purchase as permission to remain exposed.

Against Grey Talon: Use Rusted Barrel during the weapon-heavy early phase. Early Grey Talon gets substantial pressure from firing safely in the air, so reducing fire rate and bullet resistance helps you contest him.
Against Haze: Build Plated Armor for the extended weapon trade. Reducing her ability to build weapon pressure over time is more reliable than only blocking a short five-second window.

Against Infernus: Add Debuff Reducer when the burn is being reapplied constantly. Shorter debuff duration reduces the value of repeated Afterburn procs between Dispel Magic cooldowns and makes resets much easier.
Against Kelvin: Use slow resistance and movement to reach cover or break the beam angle. Keep a separate answer ready if hard control, rather than slowing, is the problem.
Against Lady Geist: Apply Decay before the finish attempt. Strong healing reduction plus current-health damage attacks the exact sustain window she relies on to survive while low.
Against Lady Geist: Build the silence before the swap can rescue her. Keep enough weapon access to apply it, rather than assuming it is a reaction after the cast.

Against McGinnis: Upgrade into Cultist Sacrifice when summon control is deciding objectives. It is a higher-commitment anti-summon answer that can remove Mini Turrets and turn entrenched turret setups into extra value instead of a permanent zone.
Against McGinnis: Use Alchemical Fire from a safe angle on grouped turrets. Its area damage can clear several parts of the setup while denying the ground McGinnis wants to hold.

Against Mo & Krill: Apply bullet-resistance reduction with coordinated weapon follow-up. The item guide source identifies Mo & Krill as a useful resistance-shred matchup; weapon damage needs access to the target to convert that reduction.

Against Rat King: Use Armor Piercer on a weapon carry or Cursed Relic if your team can commit a Tier 4 active. Armor Piercer can bypass Barriers, while Cursed Relic can strip non-ultimate barriers and buffs.

Against Rat King: Use Siphon Bullets, Scourge, Toxic Bullets, Tank Buster, or Decay depending on your build. Health-steal, percentage-health damage, and anti-heal all scale well into a high-HP Rat King.

Against Rem: Apply reliable anti-heal such as Healbane, Toxic Bullets, Decay, or Spirit Burn. Rem can produce large healing totals, so healing reduction directly attacks the reason the fight is not ending.

Against Silver: Use Return Fire during the sustained human-form weapon trade. Her rapid gun pattern can reflect meaningful damage back into her, especially on heroes that already have enough durability to stay in the exchange.
Against Vindicta: Use Phantom Strike from a hero that can safely commit. It teleports directly to her, pulls her down, and disarms her, immediately turning the range advantage into close pressure.

Against Warden: Buy Extra Stamina and preserve at least one escape charge. Warden's cage becomes much more dangerous after your stamina is reduced, so increasing the pool gives you more room for the dash-slide and heavy-melee escape.
Against a gun-focused Viscous, weapon control is conditional on the build; do not buy it simply because the spell matchup is frustrating.

Alchemical Fire helps dismantle the space an enemy team wants to fight from. Its area damage is especially useful against clustered summons: clear the setup first, then take the fight on ground that favors you.
Ally catches such as Holliday's lasso, Mo & Krill's Combo, and Dynamo's protected ultimate pressure.
